name: Fake Voxelization via Triangle-Cube Intersection
definition: A voxelization approach that voxelize every triangle of a mesh independently, checking for intersection between each triangle and axis-aligned cubes (voxels). It produces a surface representation rather than a solid interior fill, avoiding complex Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) operations.
summary: Fake Voxelization via Triangle-Cube Intersection is a surface-only technique that digitizes meshes by testing triangles against voxel templates, differing from solid methods by outputting only intersected voxels.
